summary: In Isaiah’s picture of the land’s renewal, a myrtle grows where the sirpād stood. The parallel line pictures the same change from thornbush to cypress.

senses.definition: An undesirable plant displaced by the myrtle.

evidence.note: The myrtle replaces the sirpād as part of an enduring sign for Yahweh.

cognates.note: Proposed earlier Egyptian source of the Semitic plant name. The difference in plant meanings leaves the identification uncertain.

evidence.locator: Catalogue I.17, lotus, discussion of the two directions of borrowing

note: The verse establishes the contrast with myrtle but gives no botanical description. Kilani proposes that a Middle Egyptian lotus name entered Semitic and was later borrowed back into Egyptian. Coptic ⲥⲁⲣⲡⲟⲧ means ‘lotus’. Neither that meaning nor the traditional rendering ‘nettle’ settles the species in Isaiah.
